business_model.answer: Sells senior phones and a medical-alert device plus monthly service plans, add-ons such as fall detection, and a $99/year caregiver bundle of partner services (Wellthy, AARP, Norton, Instacart). It is part of Best Buy Health; Best Buy agreed to buy its parent GreatCall for $800 million in 2018.

who_uses_who_pays.answer: The older adult carries the phone or alert device; adult children often buy it, and caregivers buy the separate caregiver subscription for themselves. The device is FSA/HSA eligible. Who pays the monthly plan is not spelled out.

evidence.quote: Got this for my Mom.

relatives_joining.answer: Yes. The device owner invites friends and family to connect through the Lively Link app, and they then get Urgent Response alerts and can see location. The caregiver bundle's Wellthy platform also lets you invite family members.

emergencies.answer: Pressing the button reaches certified US-based Urgent Response agents 24/7 who confirm location, send emergency services or call a caregiver, and stay on the line; fall detection (paid add-on) can connect automatically. What happens if the service fails is not stated.

evidence.quote: Certified agents are ready to respond in emergencies, big or small, 24/7
whether that's coordinating with emergency services or calling a caregiver or loved one to help. The agent will stay on the line until your situation is resolved.
will automatically connect you to an Urgent Response agent, even if you're unable to press the button. Requires a subscription to fall detection.

setup.answer: Buy the device online or in a store, then activate it and pick a plan online or by phone; you can keep your number. Family download the Lively Link app on their own smartphones.
